subject.title: feat: apply messages.responsePrefix to message tool outbound sends

question: Should `message(action=send)` visible sends receive the active run's provider/model/thinking context for `messages.responsePrefix` templates, or should message-tool sends remain limited to static and identity prefixes?
rationale: Current code deliberately avoids dynamic model tokens because the send path does not itself perform model selection, and plumbing that context changes the channel/tool delivery contract rather than being a narrow mechanical repair.

options.title: Design dynamic parity
options.body: Sponsor a focused design that passes the active attempt context into visible message-tool sends and covers fallback, dry-run, source-reply, and cross-target semantics before implementation.

options.title: Document static-only sends
options.body: Keep current behavior and update docs to state that message-tool sends support static and identity prefixes but not selected provider/model/thinking templates.

options.title: Fold into model-attribution work
options.body: Move this remaining dynamic-template request under the broader model-attribution product direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33975 if maintainers want one attribution surface instead of prefix-path parity.

recommendation.title: Design dynamic parity
recommendation.body: Sponsor a focused design that passes the active attempt context into visible message-tool sends and covers fallback, dry-run, source-reply, and cross-target semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the partial fix that intentionally left this policy boundary open, so they are the best available routing owner from current history.
